newsitem.title: JAPAN: Rubber - Dull trade expected, looking for direction.
newsitem.headline: Rubber - Dull trade expected, looking for direction.

text.p: Japanese rubber futures markets are likely to look for clear direction in continued dull trade this week amid a dearth of fresh incentives, Japanese traders said on Monday.

"The near-term outlook is uncertain. A view that prices were too low after the recent weaker tendency may help boost prices on technical factors, but on the other hand, prices might slip further due to pressure on near-term over supply trends," an analyst at a commodity broker said.
The benchmark September rubber futures contract on the Tokyo Commodity Exchange (TOCOM) ended the morning session at 143.3 yen per kg, against 144.9 yen on Friday.
Similarly, benchmark September contract on the Kobe Rubber Exchange was quoted at 144.6 yen per kg, compared with 145.8 yen last Friday.
Expectations that Japan's rubber stocks will rise up to around 45,000 tonnes in the near-term continue to pressure the market.
Japan's rubber stocks at the end of March rose to 39,027 tonnes, the first time that domestic stocks have broken above 39,000 tonnes since early December.
Traders said that fundamental sentiment in rubber futures markets remained bearish, even if a moderate technical rebound is possible.

"Sentiment is basically bearish on ample near-term supplies and an expected weakness in producing countries. But a perception that yen will basically weak may prevent prices from falling sharply," a trader at a trading house said.
"Expectations that rubber stocks will gain are a bearish factor. But it is uncertain how far prices will dip on the factor as it is already digested in the market to some extent," one trader said.
The offer price for Thai rubber to Japan was quoted at 116 U.S. cents per kg as of Monday, compared with 120 cents last Monday.
In the local physical market, benchmark Thai rubber for large-lot end-users was quoted at 160 yen per kg on Monday, compared with 159 yen on March 7.
